claims.hypothesis: Public PI-led ALMA archival observations in the COSMOS field can be homogeneously imaged and mined with complementary blind and prior-based photometry pipelines to produce consistent, accurate continuum flux densities.
claims.experiment: Imaged 1534 archival pointings with CASA (robust=2), extracted sources using PyBDSF (blind) and GALFIT (prior-based), and compared fluxes against each other, GILDAS uv_fit on 301 pointings, and getpix aperture photometry.
claims.result: 96% of common sources between PyBDSF and GALFIT agree within 3 sigma (mean log10 ratio -0.013 +/- 0.10 dex), and median offsets relative to uv_fit are 0.015 dex (blind) and -0.005 dex (prior).
claims.finding: Image-plane blind and prior-based continuum photometries are mutually consistent and agree well with uv-plane fitting and aperture photometry.

evidence.loc: 2.5. Comparing Blind Extraction and Prior Fitting Results
evidence.quote: 96% of sources have fluxes agreeing within 3 _σ_ .

evidence.loc: 2.6. Comparison to uv-plane Source Fitting Results
evidence.quote: The `uv_fit` flux densities and the prior-based and blind (sub-)mm photometries agree very well.

claims.hypothesis: The prior distribution of source flux densities and sizes assumed in Monte Carlo simulations significantly impacts derived flux bias corrections and error estimates.
claims.experiment: Performed two MC simulations on 150+ representative ALMA residual maps: a uniform grid simulation (FULL) and a physically motivated simulation (PHYS) based on empirical SMFs, MS relations, and galaxy size evolution.
claims.result: At low S/N_peak and small recovered sizes, the FULL simulation shows much smaller flux boosting than the PHYS simulation due to resolution bias from abundant simulated large, low-S/N sources; applying PHYS corrections yields normalized residual histograms matching a unit Gaussian.
claims.finding: Realistic input galaxy distributions (PHYS) are required to properly correct flux biases and re-estimate flux errors in ALMA continuum photometry.

evidence.loc: 3.1.1. Flux bias in the PyBDSF photometry
evidence.quote: The flux bias in the “FULL” simulation is much smaller than compared to the “PHYS” simulation. This is due to the difference of the input populations of the two simulations.

evidence.loc: C.3. Final statistical behaviour of corrected fluxes and errors
evidence.quote: The final histograms nicely agree with the mean = 0, sigma = 1 1D Gaussian.

claims.hypothesis: Multi-wavelength counterpart association for ALMA detections can be automated using supervised machine learning to replace manual visual inspection.
claims.experiment: Measured positional separation, S/N, surface brightness extension (Ext.), crowdedness, and clean parameters on HST i-band, UltraVISTA Ks, IRAC 3.6 um, and VLA 3 GHz cutouts for 1027 sources, training a scikit-learn Gaussian Process classifier on 60% of visually classified sources.
claims.result: The GP classifier achieved ~96.5% accuracy on the 40% validation set and 97% overall agreement with visual classifications, flagging 36 unreliable counterpart outliers.
claims.finding: The trained Gaussian Process classifier reliably automates counterpart association quality assessment for ALMA detections.

evidence.quote: Running our trained model on the validation sample gave an accuracy of _∼_ 96 _._ 5%.
After this automated counterpart association step, 36 sources are flagged as spurious sources

claims.hypothesis: Iterative MAGPHYS SED fitting (with energy balance and ALMA continuum constraints, iterating with and without 24 um data) provides reliable stellar masses even without an explicit AGN template component.
claims.experiment: Compared MAGPHYS stellar masses against SED3FIT stellar masses (which include an AGN component) from Delvecchio et al. (2017) for 396 common galaxies, including 158 classified AGNs.
claims.result: 391 of 396 galaxies agree within 3 sigma, with only 5 outliers outside the 3 sigma envelope.
claims.finding: Multi-run MAGPHYS SED fitting with ALMA continuum constraints yields robust stellar masses for the vast majority of galaxies, including AGN hosts.

why_this_data.value: The COSMOS field has the richest, deepest multi-wavelength datasets over 2 deg^2, and accumulated public PI-led ALMA observations cover 164 arcmin^2, exceeding the areal coverage of any contiguous ALMA deep field survey at all sensitivities.

evidence.quote: We limit our selection to within the COSMOS field (R.A. = 10:00:28.6, decl. = +02:12:21.0, J2000; Scoville et al. 2007) because it is one of the deep fields with the richest, deepest multiwavelength datasets
Given that the ALMA archival data in the COSMOS field alone cover a larger cumulative area at all sensitivities, a systematic mining of the ALMA archive is strongly motivated.

why_this_method.value: Combining blind source extraction (PyBDSF) and prior-based fitting (GALFIT) reaches deeper detection limits while identifying blended/inconsistent sources; physically-motivated MC simulations properly account for resolution and flux boosting biases.

evidence.quote: In addition to the blind source extraction, we utilize known source positions as a prior for the source fitting. This technique allows for deeper detection limits and lowers the spurious source fraction.

evidence.loc: 2.5 Comparing Blind Extraction and Prior Fitting
evidence.quote: With both PyBDSF and prior-based galfit photometry, we not only obtain accurate independent fluxes which agree very well but also identify those few (0.5% [12] ) sources which suffer from source multiplicity/blending issues.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Selecting the final sample with a total flux S/N threshold was rejected in favor of a constant S/N_peak threshold because completeness depends strongly on source size for total flux S/N.

evidence.quote: Given our finding that completeness shows an obvious dependency on source sizes, if selecting a sample with a total flux S _/_ N threshold, the sample will have different completeness for different sizes. But when selecting with a constant S _/_ N peak threshold, the sample will have a homogeneous completeness.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Using the uniform full-parameter-space (FULL) simulation for final flux bias correction was rejected in favor of the physically-motivated (PHYS) simulation because FULL underestimates flux boosting at low S/N.

evidence.quote: We choose the “PHYS” simulation for the final correction, considering the discussion in the previous sections, i.e., “PHYS” simulation is more representative of our real data. Note that using “FULL” simulation would underestimate the flux bias correction

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Direct blanking of line-contaminated channels before continuum imaging was rejected in favor of post-facto empirical line prediction and subtraction to avoid massive data volume, analysis time, and dataset inhomogeneity.

referee_caveats_inferred: Aggregating all spectral windows into continuum images without prior line flagging means any unpredicted or anomalously bright emission line (or line in a source with an inaccurate photo-z) directly biases the continuum flux density.

Using a single scalar primary beam attenuation factor evaluated at the source center can bias total flux measurements for extended sources located far from the phase center where the primary beam gradient is steep.

Training and validating the Gaussian Process counterpart classifier on visual inspections of the same 1027-source dataset risks overfitting to the specific depth and resolution distribution of v20180102.
